Front:
A team needs a central Azure resource for jobs, assets, compute, and access control used by its machine learning project. What should it create?

A) An Azure Machine Learning workspace
B) A Microsoft Foundry project resource
C) An Azure AI Search service
Back:
A) An Azure Machine Learning workspace

A Machine Learning workspace is the top-level resource for coordinating Azure Machine Learning jobs, assets, compute, and security.

Reference: Azure Machine Learning workspace
Extra: A workspace governs the ML lifecycle. A Foundry project organizes generative AI development, while AI Search indexes and retrieves content rather than managing ML training operations.

Front:
Training jobs must access an existing ADLS Gen2 location without copying its files into the workspace. Which workspace object should reference it?

A) A versioned data asset
B) An Azure Machine Learning datastore
C) An Azure Machine Learning environment
Back:
B) An Azure Machine Learning datastore

A datastore securely stores connection information that lets jobs access an external storage service.

Reference: Create and manage datastores
Extra: A datastore represents the storage connection; a data asset identifies particular data within storage. An environment defines runtime dependencies and cannot provide storage connectivity.

Front:
A nightly training workload needs multiple CPU nodes only while jobs run and must scale to zero afterward. Which compute target is best?

A) A permanently running compute instance
B) An attached Azure Kubernetes cluster
C) A managed compute cluster with minimum nodes set to zero
Back:
C) A managed compute cluster with minimum nodes set to zero

A managed compute cluster can autoscale across nodes and deallocate all nodes when idle.

Reference: Create a compute cluster
Extra: Compute instances suit interactive development and remain single-node. Attached Kubernetes is appropriate when the organization needs cluster control, but adds operational overhead for an elastic training requirement.

Front:
A data scientist needs an individually managed cloud workstation for notebooks, terminals, and interactive debugging. Which target should be provisioned?

A) An Azure Machine Learning compute instance
B) An Azure Machine Learning compute cluster
C) An Azure Machine Learning batch endpoint
Back:
A) An Azure Machine Learning compute instance

A compute instance is a managed development environment intended for interactive work by an individual user.

Reference: Compute instance
Extra: A compute cluster is optimized for scalable job execution, while a batch endpoint performs asynchronous inference. Use instances for authoring and clusters for repeatable production runs.

Front:
A pipeline must read blobs without storing account keys in code. Security requires revocable Azure authorization and least privilege. What should be configured?

A) A shared access signature embedded in the component YAML
B) The workspace managed identity with an appropriate data-plane role
C) The storage account key saved as a GitHub repository secret
Back:
B) The workspace managed identity with an appropriate data-plane role

Managed identity plus Azure RBAC enables credential-free access and narrowly scoped authorization.

Reference: Authentication with managed identities
Extra: SAS tokens and account keys are secrets that require rotation and can be overprivileged. Managed identity removes secret distribution while RBAC controls the exact storage scope and actions.

Front:
A curated training folder must be referenced by a stable name, versioned when its definition changes, and mounted by jobs. Which asset type fits?

A) A uri_folder data asset
B) A custom Docker environment
C) A registered MLflow model
Back:
A) A uri_folder data asset

A uri_folder data asset creates a versioned reference to a folder that jobs can download or mount.

Reference: Create data assets
Extra: Data assets describe inputs and preserve lineage without necessarily duplicating data. Environments package dependencies; models package inference artifacts rather than source training folders.

Front:
Training must use the same Python and CUDA dependencies in development and CI runs. Which reusable asset should the team version?

A) A compute instance schedule
B) An Azure Machine Learning environment
C) A workspace diagnostic setting
Back:
B) An Azure Machine Learning environment

An environment versions the Docker image and Python dependencies used to execute jobs consistently.

Reference: Manage environments
Extra: Compute schedules control availability and diagnostic settings route logs. Environments address runtime reproducibility and should be pinned to explicit versions in production jobs.

Front:
A preprocessing step will be reused in several pipelines and must declare inputs, outputs, code, and runtime independently. What should be created?

A) A reusable command component
B) A standalone online deployment
C) A storage lifecycle policy
Back:
A) A reusable command component

A component packages executable logic with its interface and environment for reuse in pipelines.

Reference: Azure Machine Learning components
Extra: Components are modular pipeline building blocks that support versioning and lineage. Online deployments serve requests, and lifecycle policies manage stored objects rather than ML workflow logic.

Front:
Two workspaces in different subscriptions must consume the same approved models, components, and environments. Which service should hold these assets?

A) A shared Azure Machine Learning registry
B) A shared Log Analytics workspace
C) A shared Azure Container Registry repository only
Back:
A) A shared Azure Machine Learning registry

A registry shares versioned Machine Learning assets across workspaces and organizational boundaries.

Reference: Manage Azure Machine Learning registries
Extra: A container registry shares images but not complete ML asset metadata, lineage, models, and components. Log Analytics centralizes telemetry rather than reusable ML assets.

Front:
A GitHub Actions workflow must submit Azure ML jobs without a long-lived client secret. Which authentication pattern should be used?

A) A storage account access key in GitHub secrets
B) OpenID Connect federation with an Azure identity
C) A workspace user token committed to the repository
Back:
B) OpenID Connect federation with an Azure identity

GitHub OIDC federation exchanges a short-lived token for Azure access and avoids stored client credentials.

Reference: Connect GitHub Actions to Azure with OpenID Connect
Extra: OIDC reduces secret rotation and leakage risk. Storage keys do not authenticate Azure Resource Manager operations, and user tokens are unsuitable for unattended automation.

Front:
Development and production workspaces must be recreated consistently through pull requests. Which approach provides declarative and repeatable resource deployment?

A) Manual creation in Azure portal with screenshots
B) An Azure CLI script containing interactive prompts
C) Version-controlled Bicep modules with parameter files
Back:
C) Version-controlled Bicep modules with parameter files

Bicep provides declarative Azure infrastructure definitions that can be reviewed, parameterized, and repeatedly deployed.

Reference: Bicep overview
Extra: Portal steps are difficult to audit and reproduce. CLI can be automated, but interactive imperative scripts provide weaker desired-state semantics than parameterized Bicep modules.

Front:
Infrastructure changes must be validated on pull requests and deployed only after merge to the main branch. What should orchestrate this policy?

A) A recurring Azure Machine Learning pipeline schedule
B) Separate GitHub Actions workflows triggered by pull_request and push
C) A notebook that an administrator runs after each merge
Back:
B) Separate GitHub Actions workflows triggered by pull_request and push

GitHub Actions event triggers can validate proposed IaC on pull requests and deploy approved changes after a push to the protected branch.

Reference: Use GitHub Actions with Azure Machine Learning
Extra: ML pipeline schedules orchestrate model workflows, not repository governance. Manual notebooks weaken auditability; protected branches plus event-driven workflows separate validation from deployment.

Front:
An Azure ML workspace must be reachable only from approved virtual networks while public access is disabled. Which configuration meets the requirement?

A) A private endpoint with private DNS integration
B) A public endpoint protected only by resource locks
C) A service health alert scoped to the workspace
Back:
A) A private endpoint with private DNS integration

Private Link exposes the workspace through a private IP, while private DNS resolves workspace endpoints inside the virtual network.

Reference: Configure a private endpoint
Extra: Resource locks prevent deletion or modification but do not filter network traffic. Health alerts report platform issues and provide no network isolation.

Front:
A team needs reviewable history for training code, component YAML, and environment definitions while large datasets remain in cloud storage. What should be placed in Git?

A) Source and declarative definitions, excluding data and generated artifacts
B) Every training dataset and model binary in normal Git objects
C) Only notebook outputs, excluding scripts and configuration files
Back:
A) Source and declarative definitions, excluding data and generated artifacts

Git should track code and configuration; durable data and large model artifacts belong in managed data and model stores.

Reference: Git integration for Azure Machine Learning
Extra: Committing large data bloats repository history and risks data exposure. Notebook outputs are generated state; the reproducible inputs—code and definitions—are the important reviewable assets.

Front:
A datastore accesses ADLS Gen2 through the identity of each interactive user, so storage permissions must differ by user. Which datastore authentication mode is appropriate?

A) Account-key authentication shared by every user
B) Identity-based authentication with user credentials
C) Anonymous public-container authentication
Back:
B) Identity-based authentication with user credentials

Identity-based access can pass through the signed-in user's identity so storage RBAC determines individual authorization.

Reference: Data authentication administration
Extra: A shared key erases per-user accountability and grants common privileges. Anonymous access cannot enforce identity-specific permissions and is inappropriate for protected training data.

Front:
A CPU cluster is idle most weekends but receives unpredictable weekday jobs. How should it minimize cost without delaying cluster recreation?

A) Delete and redeploy the cluster after every job
B) Keep one node running continuously for readiness
C) Set minimum nodes to zero and configure an idle timeout
Back:
C) Set minimum nodes to zero and configure an idle timeout

Autoscaling to zero releases compute cost after the configured idle period while preserving the cluster definition.

Reference: Configure compute cluster autoscaling
Extra: Deleting infrastructure adds provisioning overhead and operational churn. A permanent node reduces startup latency but violates the cost-minimization requirement during long idle periods.

Front:
A production job unexpectedly changes behavior after a curated environment receives a new version. Which practice best preserves reproducibility?

A) Reference the environment by name and explicit version
B) Resolve the newest environment version at each run
C) Rebuild dependencies from unpinned package names
Back:
A) Reference the environment by name and explicit version

Pinning the environment asset version gives each job a stable and auditable runtime definition.

Reference: Manage environment versions
Extra: Using latest introduces silent runtime changes. Unpinned package resolution is even less deterministic because upstream packages can change without an Azure ML asset update.

Front:
A pipeline step is unchanged, but teams repeatedly copy its YAML and code into new projects. Which action best improves governance and reuse?

A) Convert the step into a versioned component
B) Convert the step into an online endpoint
C) Convert the step into a datastore credential
Back:
A) Convert the step into a versioned component

A versioned component exposes a stable contract and can be reused without duplicating implementation details.

Reference: Machine Learning component concepts
Extra: Endpoints host inference and datastores provide storage connections. Neither supplies the composable interface, lineage, and runtime encapsulation needed for pipeline reuse.

Front:
A central platform team publishes an approved model, and regional workspaces must consume that exact version without separate copies owned by each team. What should they reference?

A) A model asset in a Machine Learning registry
B) A model file attached to a GitHub release
C) A model output inside one workspace job
Back:
A) A model asset in a Machine Learning registry

Registry assets are centrally versioned and can be referenced from jobs or deployments in multiple workspaces.

Reference: Manage models in registries
Extra: GitHub releases lack Azure ML deployment metadata and governance. A job output is scoped operational state until it is registered and is not a governed cross-workspace contract.

Front:
A training script logs parameters, metrics, and artifacts, and analysts need a standard experiment UI without custom tracking infrastructure. What should be integrated?

A) MLflow tracking in Azure Machine Learning
B) Azure Policy compliance scan results
C) Azure Storage lifecycle management
Back:
A) MLflow tracking in Azure Machine Learning

Azure ML integrates with MLflow to record runs, parameters, metrics, and artifacts in workspace experiments.

Reference: MLflow and Azure Machine Learning
Extra: Policy evaluates resource compliance, and storage lifecycle rules move or delete blobs. Neither provides experiment semantics or comparison of model-training runs.

Front:
A supported scikit-learn training script needs automatic capture of common parameters, metrics, and model artifacts with minimal logging code. Which MLflow capability should be enabled?

A) Model serving with a batch endpoint
B) MLflow autologging for the framework
C) Data drift monitoring on the input asset
Back:
B) MLflow autologging for the framework

MLflow autologging automatically records framework-specific training information and artifacts.

Reference: Log and view metrics with MLflow
Extra: Serving and drift monitoring happen after or outside training. Autologging reduces instrumentation effort, though explicit logging remains useful for custom business metrics.

Front:
A team wants Azure to test preprocessing and algorithm combinations for a labeled tabular classification dataset under a time budget. Which capability is appropriate?

A) Automated machine learning classification
B) A manual sweep over one script parameter
C) A responsible AI dashboard for one model
Back:
A) Automated machine learning classification

Automated ML explores supported algorithms and featurization choices while honoring experiment constraints.

Reference: Automated machine learning
Extra: A sweep tunes parameters defined by the author but does not broadly select algorithms and preprocessing. A responsible AI dashboard analyzes an existing model rather than searching candidates.

Front:
A data scientist is exploring distributions and debugging feature code interactively before converting the work into a repeatable job. Which tool is most suitable now?

A) A managed online endpoint deployment
B) A notebook on a compute instance
C) A scheduled batch endpoint invocation
Back:
B) A notebook on a compute instance

Notebooks provide interactive code execution and visualization for exploration on managed development compute.

Reference: Run Jupyter notebooks
Extra: Endpoints are production inference interfaces and do not provide an exploratory authoring loop. Once exploration stabilizes, move logic into scripts and components for reproducibility.

Front:
A training job must evaluate learning rate and batch size combinations in parallel and select the run with the best validation score. What should be submitted?

A) A hyperparameter sweep job
B) A model monitor definition
C) A managed feature store materialization job
Back:
A) A hyperparameter sweep job

A sweep job samples a defined parameter space and optimizes child runs against a primary metric.

Reference: Tune hyperparameters
Extra: Model monitoring evaluates production behavior, while feature materialization computes feature values. Neither launches comparative training trials against an optimization metric.

Front:
Many weak hyperparameter trials consume the full budget even after their metric is clearly worse than leading runs. Which change reduces wasted compute?

A) Increase the maximum nodes of the cluster
B) Configure an early termination policy
C) Disable the primary optimization metric
Back:
B) Configure an early termination policy

An early termination policy stops poorly performing child runs according to intermediate metric results.

Reference: Early termination of sweep runs
Extra: More nodes increase concurrency but not efficiency per trial. The primary metric is required to compare runs; early termination conserves budget without eliminating optimization guidance.

Front:
Production training must execute a Python script noninteractively with declared inputs, outputs, environment, and compute. Which Azure ML job type is the direct fit?

A) A command job
B) An interactive notebook session
C) An online inference request
Back:
A) A command job

A command job runs a specified command on managed compute with explicit data and environment dependencies.

Reference: Train models with jobs
Extra: Notebooks are suited to exploration and can hide state. Online requests invoke deployed inference; they do not provide repeatable training execution and output lineage.

Front:
A deep learning job no longer fits efficiently on one GPU and must coordinate training across several GPU nodes. What should the job configure?

A) A parallel distribution strategy such as PyTorch or MPI
B) A larger batch endpoint retry count
C) A semantic ranker configuration for the dataset
Back:
A) A parallel distribution strategy such as PyTorch or MPI

Azure ML distribution settings launch and coordinate processes across GPUs and nodes for supported frameworks.

Reference: Distributed training
Extra: Endpoint retries concern inference reliability, and semantic ranking concerns search relevance. Distributed training also requires code and framework behavior compatible with multi-process execution.

Front:
Data preparation, training, and evaluation must execute as a dependency graph with reusable steps and recorded lineage. What should the team build?

A) A sequence of portal operations documented in a wiki
B) An Azure Machine Learning pipeline job
C) A single long-running online deployment
Back:
B) An Azure Machine Learning pipeline job

A pipeline composes components into a directed workflow with dependencies, inputs, outputs, and lineage.

Reference: Machine Learning pipelines
Extra: Manual portal actions are not repeatable, and online deployments serve predictions rather than orchestrating training stages. Components keep pipeline steps independently reusable.

Front:
A pipeline reruns daily, but an expensive preprocessing component should reuse prior output whenever its code, environment, and inputs are unchanged. Which feature helps?

A) Component output reuse in the pipeline
B) Online endpoint traffic mirroring
C) Workspace soft-delete protection
Back:
A) Component output reuse in the pipeline

Azure ML can reuse a prior component result when the step definition and relevant inputs remain unchanged.

Reference: Pipeline reuse
Extra: Traffic mirroring validates deployments, and soft delete protects resources. Neither avoids repeated deterministic pipeline computation; disable reuse only for genuinely nondeterministic steps.

Front:
Twenty training runs used different parameters. The team needs to sort them by validation AUC and inspect metrics side by side. Which mechanism should it use?

A) Experiment run comparison using logged MLflow metrics
B) Storage account metrics grouped by container
C) Endpoint access logs grouped by status code
Back:
A) Experiment run comparison using logged MLflow metrics

Logged runs can be queried and compared by metrics and parameters to identify candidate models.

Reference: Track experiments with MLflow
Extra: Storage and endpoint telemetry describe infrastructure and serving behavior, not validation quality across training candidates. Consistent metric names are essential for reliable comparisons.

Front:
An online model requires point-in-time feature retrieval at inference, and its retrieval definition must travel with the model artifact. What should registration include?

A) A packaged feature retrieval specification
B) A compute cluster autoscale schedule
C) A workspace private DNS zone export
Back:
A) A packaged feature retrieval specification

Packaging the retrieval specification with the model preserves the feature contract needed for consistent serving.

Reference: Managed feature store concepts
Extra: Autoscale and DNS settings govern infrastructure, not feature semantics. Coupling the retrieval specification to the model reduces training-serving skew and improves deployment reproducibility.

Front:
A model logged during training must become a governed, versioned workspace asset that can be deployed later. Which action is required?

A) Register the MLflow model in Azure Machine Learning
B) Leave the artifact only in the temporary run output
C) Copy the pickle file into the source repository
Back:
A) Register the MLflow model in Azure Machine Learning

Registration creates a named and versioned model asset from the MLflow artifact.

Reference: Manage MLflow models
Extra: Run outputs provide lineage but are not the promoted deployment contract. Git is unsuitable for large binaries and lacks Azure ML model lifecycle metadata.

Front:
A retrained model uses the same logical name but must coexist with the currently deployed model until validation finishes. How should it be registered?

A) Overwrite the deployed model files in place
B) Create a new version under the same model name
C) Rename the workspace before every retraining run
Back:
B) Create a new version under the same model name

Model versions preserve immutable candidates under a stable logical name for comparison and controlled promotion.

Reference: Register and manage model versions
Extra: In-place mutation destroys provenance and rollback safety. Workspace renaming does not version an artifact and disrupts dependent automation.

Front:
Before promoting a loan model, reviewers must inspect performance disparities across demographic cohorts and understand influential features. Which capability should they use?

A) Responsible AI dashboard analysis
B) Compute cluster node diagnostics
C) Azure Resource Graph inventory
Back:
A) Responsible AI dashboard analysis

The Responsible AI dashboard combines model explanations, error analysis, and fairness-oriented cohort assessment.

Reference: Responsible AI dashboard
Extra: Compute diagnostics investigate infrastructure, while Resource Graph inventories Azure resources. Responsible evaluation complements—not replaces—domain review and governance decisions.

Front:
An obsolete model must no longer appear in normal active-model workflows, but audit history and lineage must be retained. What should be done?

A) Delete every run and artifact permanently
B) Archive the registered model asset
C) Move the workspace to another subscription
Back:
B) Archive the registered model asset

Archiving removes an asset from active use while preserving its metadata and history for governance.

Reference: Manage the model lifecycle
Extra: Permanent deletion conflicts with retention and audit requirements. Subscription movement changes resource ownership but does not express lifecycle status for the model.

Front:
A fraud-scoring API must return one prediction synchronously for each request with low latency. Which deployment target is appropriate?

A) A managed online endpoint
B) A recurring batch endpoint job
C) A training pipeline schedule
Back:
A) A managed online endpoint

Online endpoints provide synchronous request-response inference for low-latency applications.

Reference: Online endpoints
Extra: Batch endpoints process large asynchronous datasets and do not serve interactive calls. Pipeline schedules orchestrate workflows rather than expose inference APIs.

Front:
A retailer scores 50 million records overnight and writes results to storage; no caller waits for an immediate response. Which target should it use?

A) A managed online endpoint with one request per row
B) An Azure Machine Learning batch endpoint
C) A compute instance running an open notebook
Back:
B) An Azure Machine Learning batch endpoint

Batch endpoints provide asynchronous, scalable inference over large datasets and persist outputs.

Reference: Batch endpoints
Extra: Online endpoints add per-request overhead for an offline workload. An interactive notebook lacks production scheduling, isolation, retry, and scalable parallel execution.

Front:
A team wants Azure to provision and patch the inference infrastructure while it controls deployment instances and scaling. Which option minimizes operational burden?

A) A managed online endpoint
B) A self-managed Kubernetes web service
C) A virtual machine with a custom API daemon
Back:
A) A managed online endpoint

Managed online endpoints handle serving infrastructure while exposing deployment, instance, traffic, and scaling controls.

Reference: Managed online endpoints
Extra: Kubernetes and VMs offer more infrastructure control but require cluster or host operations. Choose them only when requirements justify that additional responsibility.

Front:
A new online deployment returns HTTP 500 responses. The team needs container startup output and scoring-script exceptions. What should it inspect first?

A) Deployment logs for the managed online endpoint
B) The model card description in the registry
C) Git branch protection audit events
Back:
A) Deployment logs for the managed online endpoint

Deployment logs expose container initialization and scoring failures needed to diagnose unhealthy inference replicas.

Reference: Troubleshoot online endpoints
Extra: Model descriptions and Git governance do not show runtime exceptions. Also validate locally and invoke the endpoint with representative payloads before shifting production traffic.

Front:
A replacement model must receive 10% of production requests while the current model receives 90%, with both behind one endpoint URL. What should be configured?

A) Weighted traffic allocation across two deployments
B) Two unrelated workspaces with separate DNS names
C) A batch deployment with ten parallel workers
Back:
A) Weighted traffic allocation across two deployments

An online endpoint can split traffic by percentage among deployments to support controlled rollout.

Reference: Safely roll out online endpoints
Extra: Separate endpoints complicate client routing and measurement. Batch worker count controls parallel offline processing, not request allocation between model versions.

Front:
A team wants to observe how a candidate deployment responds to live requests without returning its predictions to callers. Which rollout technique should it use?

A) Mirrored traffic to the candidate deployment
B) Fifty-percent weighted production traffic
C) A permanent batch scoring schedule
Back:
A) Mirrored traffic to the candidate deployment

Traffic mirroring sends copies of requests to a deployment while excluding its responses from client results.

Reference: Mirror online endpoint traffic
Extra: Weighted traffic exposes users to candidate responses, which violates the constraint. Batch scoring cannot reproduce live request shape, timing, or serving conditions.

Front:
Error rate rises immediately after all endpoint traffic moves to the new deployment. The old deployment is still healthy. What is the fastest safe response?

A) Retrain the new model while it serves all traffic
B) Reallocate traffic to the previous deployment
C) Delete the endpoint and create a different workspace
Back:
B) Reallocate traffic to the previous deployment

Keeping the prior deployment available enables rapid rollback by changing endpoint traffic weights.

Reference: Rollback an online deployment
Extra: Retraining does not immediately protect users, and endpoint deletion creates unnecessary downtime. Define health thresholds and automated rollback criteria before rollout.

Front:
A model's input distributions may change after deployment even though ground-truth labels arrive weeks later. Which signal can detect this earliest?

A) Data drift between baseline and production inputs
B) Workspace resource-group naming drift
C) Git commit frequency for training scripts
Back:
A) Data drift between baseline and production inputs

Data drift monitoring compares production feature distributions with a reference dataset without requiring immediate labels.

Reference: Model monitoring
Extra: Infrastructure naming and source activity do not measure statistical changes in model inputs. Drift signals risk; it does not by itself prove that predictive quality declined.

Front:
Labels for production predictions are available. Which measure most directly reveals whether a classifier's quality has degraded?

A) Prediction performance metrics computed against ground truth
B) Average CPU utilization of inference replicas
C) Number of registered environment versions
Back:
A) Prediction performance metrics computed against ground truth

Comparing predictions with ground truth enables direct monitoring of quality metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, or AUC.

Reference: Monitor model performance
Extra: CPU utilization indicates infrastructure load, not correctness. Asset counts are governance metadata; neither can establish predictive degradation.

Front:
A production model should be checked every day against a recent data window without manual execution. What should the team configure?

A) A scheduled model monitoring job
B) An always-open notebook kernel
C) A repository issue template
Back:
A) A scheduled model monitoring job

A scheduled monitor repeatedly computes configured signals over production data and baseline windows.

Reference: Configure model monitoring
Extra: Notebook kernels are interactive and fragile for operations, while issue templates only standardize human reports. Monitoring schedules should align with data arrival and business response time.

Front:
Retraining is costly and must start only after a drift metric exceeds the approved limit, while operators must also be notified. Which design is best?

A) Trigger an alert and an automated retraining workflow from the threshold breach
B) Retrain continuously after every individual prediction
C) Wait for an annual manual review regardless of the metric
Back:
A) Trigger an alert and an automated retraining workflow from the threshold breach

Threshold-driven automation links monitored degradation to timely notification and controlled retraining.

Reference: Production model monitoring
Extra: Per-prediction retraining is wasteful and unstable, while annual review ignores the required response. Promotion should still require evaluation gates rather than automatically replacing production.

Front:
A batch deployment processes many independent files too slowly on one node. The scoring code already supports mini-batches. Which change improves throughput?

A) Increase batch parallelism and instance count
B) Convert the workload into one synchronous request
C) Disable partitioning of the input dataset
Back:
A) Increase batch parallelism and instance count

Batch deployments can divide input into mini-batches and process them concurrently across compute instances.

Reference: Use batch model deployments
Extra: One synchronous request sacrifices batch scalability and risks timeout. Disabling partitioning prevents parallel work distribution and worsens the bottleneck.

Front:
Only approved callers should invoke a managed online endpoint, and keys must not be distributed. Which authentication mode best fits?

A) Microsoft Entra token authentication
B) Anonymous public access
C) A shared endpoint key in source control
Back:
A) Microsoft Entra token authentication

Microsoft Entra authentication supports identity-based access and avoids distributing static endpoint keys.

Reference: Authenticate clients for online endpoints
Extra: Anonymous access cannot enforce caller identity, and committed keys are easily leaked and shared. Pair identity authentication with least-privilege role assignments.

Front:
A batch endpoint invocation failed on several mini-batches because input files were malformed. Where should operators look for per-job failure details?

A) The batch job logs and output/error artifacts
B) The workspace's model description field
C) The repository's pull request labels
Back:
A) The batch job logs and output/error artifacts

Each batch invocation creates a job whose logs and artifacts expose scoring and mini-batch failures.

Reference: Troubleshoot batch endpoints
Extra: Model metadata and PR labels cannot reveal runtime parsing errors. A robust scoring script should log failed items and define retry/error-threshold behavior deliberately.

Front:
A team must promote only models whose test metric exceeds 0.90 and whose responsible AI review is approved. Where should this decision be enforced?

A) In an automated deployment gate before production traffic changes
B) In the endpoint description after deployment completes
C) In a compute instance startup script for each developer
Back:
A) In an automated deployment gate before production traffic changes

A release gate can evaluate model metrics and governance approvals before a candidate is promoted.

Reference: Machine learning operations process
Extra: Descriptions document state but do not enforce it, and developer startup scripts are not centralized release controls. Keep evaluation evidence immutable and tied to the registered model version.

Front:
The same pipeline definition must run with different datasets in development and production without editing component code. What design supports this?

A) Parameterize pipeline inputs and environment-specific bindings
B) Hard-code production storage paths in every component
C) Duplicate the entire pipeline for each dataset version
Back:
A) Parameterize pipeline inputs and environment-specific bindings

Explicit pipeline inputs separate reusable workflow logic from environment-specific data references.

Reference: Create component pipelines
Extra: Hard-coding reduces portability and may expose production paths. Duplication causes configuration drift; parameterization preserves one governed workflow definition.

Front:
A model candidate has better aggregate accuracy but performs substantially worse for a protected cohort. What should block automatic promotion?

A) A responsible AI acceptance criterion for cohort performance
B) A lower compute-cluster idle timeout
C) A newer Docker base image tag
Back:
A) A responsible AI acceptance criterion for cohort performance

Promotion criteria should include disaggregated performance and fairness risks, not only aggregate quality.

Reference: Responsible AI assessment
Extra: Compute cost and image freshness matter operationally but do not resolve harmful cohort disparity. Human governance should define acceptable tradeoffs and escalation paths.

Front:
A Foundry team needs a governed boundary for connections, deployments, agents, evaluations, and collaborators for one application. What should it create?

A) A Microsoft Foundry project
B) An Azure Machine Learning datastore
C) An Azure Monitor action group
Back:
A) A Microsoft Foundry project

A Foundry project organizes application resources, connections, deployments, assets, and team access.

Reference: What is Microsoft Foundry
Extra: A datastore abstracts storage connectivity, while an action group routes alerts. Neither provides the application development and governance boundary required here.

Front:
A Foundry application must access Azure AI Search without API keys. Which configuration is preferred?

A) A managed identity assigned an appropriate Search data role
B) An admin key embedded in the system prompt
C) A query key committed to the application repository
Back:
A) A managed identity assigned an appropriate Search data role

Managed identity and Azure RBAC provide credential-free, least-privilege access to the search service.

Reference: Use managed identities in Foundry
Extra: Admin keys grant broad privileges and prompts can leak. Query keys are less privileged but remain static secrets requiring distribution and rotation.

Front:
A developer should build and evaluate a Foundry application but must not change project role assignments. Which access design follows least privilege?

A) Assign the narrow project-level development role needed
B) Assign Owner at the subscription scope
C) Share the project administrator's access token
Back:
A) Assign the narrow project-level development role needed

Azure RBAC should grant only required actions at the smallest practical scope.

Reference: Role-based access control in Foundry
Extra: Subscription Owner can modify access across unrelated resources, and token sharing destroys identity and audit boundaries. Separate resource administration from application development duties.

Front:
A regulated Foundry deployment must keep service traffic on private IP addresses and disable public network access. What should be implemented?

A) Private endpoints and correctly linked private DNS zones
B) Public endpoints protected only by randomized names
C) Resource locks on every project and deployment
Back:
A) Private endpoints and correctly linked private DNS zones

Private Link and DNS integration route supported service access privately from approved networks.

Reference: Configure private networking for Foundry
Extra: Obscure names are not a security boundary, and resource locks prevent changes rather than network access. Validate every dependency because private networking must cover the complete data path.

Front:
Development, test, and production Foundry environments must use identical topology but different names and capacities. Which deployment method is best?

A) Parameterized Bicep templates invoked by automation
B) Repeated manual portal configuration in each environment
C) Exported screenshots stored with the application source
Back:
A) Parameterized Bicep templates invoked by automation

Parameterized IaC keeps topology consistent while allowing controlled environment-specific values.

Reference: Create Foundry resources with templates
Extra: Manual recreation encourages drift, and screenshots are documentation rather than executable desired state. Validate changes with what-if before deployment.

Front:
A team wants to call a catalog model through a provider-managed API and avoid managing virtual machines or containers. Which deployment type should it choose?

A) A serverless API deployment
B) A self-hosted Kubernetes deployment
C) A local compute instance deployment
Back:
A) A serverless API deployment

Serverless API deployments expose supported catalog models as managed endpoints without customer-managed serving infrastructure.

Reference: Deploy models as serverless APIs
Extra: Kubernetes is appropriate for custom infrastructure control but adds operations. A compute instance is an interactive development machine, not a production serving service.

Front:
A specialized model requires a custom inference environment and dedicated compute sizing not offered by its serverless option. Which deployment approach fits?

A) Managed compute deployment in Foundry
B) A prompt asset with no model deployment
C) A Log Analytics saved query
Back:
A) Managed compute deployment in Foundry

Managed compute supports model serving with selected compute and deployment configuration when serverless APIs do not meet requirements.

Reference: Deploy models to managed compute
Extra: Prompts orchestrate model behavior but do not host model weights. Saved queries analyze telemetry and cannot execute inference.

Front:
A customer-support application prioritizes instruction following, supported context length, regional availability, and cost. How should the team choose a foundation model?

A) Evaluate eligible catalog models against representative tasks and constraints
B) Select the model with the largest parameter count automatically
C) Select whichever model was added to the catalog most recently
Back:
A) Evaluate eligible catalog models against representative tasks and constraints

Model selection should combine workload requirements, availability, safety, quality evaluation, latency, and cost.

Reference: Models in Microsoft Foundry
Extra: Parameter count and release date are weak proxies and may conflict with cost, region, context, or latency requirements. Representative evaluation provides workload-specific evidence.

Front:
A provider announces a new model version, but production must remain reproducible until regression tests pass. What should the deployment reference?

A) An explicitly selected model version
B) An automatically resolved latest alias only
C) An unversioned model name stored in a notebook cell
Back:
A) An explicitly selected model version

Pinning a model version prevents unreviewed provider updates from silently changing production behavior.

Reference: Model versions and upgrades
Extra: Latest-style resolution trades control for convenience. Use a staged deployment and evaluation suite before deliberately promoting a newer model version.

Front:
A new foundation-model deployment must be tested with a small share of users and rolled back quickly if quality falls. Which strategy is appropriate?

A) A canary rollout with measured promotion gates
B) Immediate replacement of the only production deployment
C) Manual prompt edits directly in the production portal
Back:
A) A canary rollout with measured promotion gates

A canary strategy limits exposure, compares production signals, and retains a known-good rollback target.

Reference: Safe deployment practices
Extra: Immediate replacement increases blast radius. Unversioned portal edits bypass review and make attribution or rollback difficult.

Front:
A high-volume generative AI workload needs predictable reserved capacity and stable latency rather than consumption-based shared throughput. What should be configured?

A) Provisioned throughput units
B) A larger Log Analytics retention period
C) A higher Azure AI Search replica count only
Back:
A) Provisioned throughput units

Provisioned throughput reserves model-processing capacity for predictable high-volume workloads.

Reference: Provisioned throughput
Extra: Telemetry retention does not affect inference capacity, and search replicas improve retrieval throughput rather than language-model token processing.

Front:
Traffic is intermittent and low, and the application can tolerate variable shared-service latency. Which capacity model generally avoids paying for reserved model throughput?

A) Standard consumption-based deployment
B) Provisioned throughput deployment
C) Dedicated GPU virtual machines kept online
Back:
A) Standard consumption-based deployment

Standard deployments charge for usage and are often appropriate for variable workloads that do not justify reserved capacity.

Reference: Azure OpenAI deployment types
Extra: Provisioned throughput targets predictable sustained demand, while dedicated VMs add management and idle cost. Validate regional availability and quota before choosing a type.

Front:
A planned PTU deployment fails despite valid Bicep syntax because the subscription cannot allocate the requested model capacity in that region. What should be checked?

A) Model quota and capacity availability for the region
B) The Git repository's default branch name
C) The prompt's groundedness evaluation score
Back:
A) Model quota and capacity availability for the region

Model deployments depend on subscription quota and available capacity for the chosen model, version, type, and region.

Reference: Azure OpenAI quota and limits
Extra: Branch naming and prompt quality cannot resolve resource allocation failure. Capacity planning should precede production-region selection and IaC rollout.

Front:
A prompt change must be reviewed, reproduced, and correlated with evaluation results. How should the prompt be managed?

A) Store the prompt as a version-controlled source artifact
B) Edit only the live deployment with no saved history
C) Save the prompt in a developer's terminal history
Back:
A) Store the prompt as a version-controlled source artifact

Git-based prompt management provides history, review, branching, and linkage to tests and releases.

Reference: Develop and manage generative AI flows
Extra: Direct production edits and shell history lack governed review and reproducibility. Treat prompts, model settings, tools, and evaluation data as coordinated release inputs.

Front:
Two system prompts differ in tone and instruction ordering. The team needs objective evidence about which performs better. What should it do?

A) Evaluate both variants on the same representative dataset and metrics
B) Compare only the character count of each prompt
C) Deploy the newer prompt to all users without a baseline
Back:
A) Evaluate both variants on the same representative dataset and metrics

Controlled evaluation isolates prompt variation while holding test examples and scoring criteria constant.

Reference: Evaluate generative AI applications
Extra: Prompt length is a cost signal, not a quality verdict. Full deployment without baseline evidence increases risk and prevents a controlled comparison.

Front:
Developers frequently overwrite one another's prompt changes and cannot reproduce the version used in last week's release. Which practice fixes both issues?

A) Branch, review, and tag prompt files in Git
B) Share one mutable prompt in a team chat message
C) Put the latest prompt only in an endpoint description
Back:
A) Branch, review, and tag prompt files in Git

Git workflows preserve immutable history and enable collaborative review and release tagging.

Reference: What is version control
Extra: Chat and descriptions are mutable communication surfaces, not source-control systems. Release tags should identify prompt, configuration, and model versions together.

Front:
A production agent calls Azure services on behalf of the application. Credentials must rotate automatically and each call must be attributable to the workload. What should it use?

A) The project's managed identity with scoped RBAC
B) A developer's personal access token
C) A subscription key pasted into agent instructions
Back:
A) The project's managed identity with scoped RBAC

A managed workload identity supplies short-lived tokens and auditable authorization without embedded secrets.

Reference: Managed identity for Foundry projects
Extra: Personal tokens couple production to a person, and prompts are unsafe secret stores. Scope each tool's permissions independently where practical.

Front:
A Foundry project needs governed access to an existing Azure AI Search service used by its RAG application. Which project object should represent that dependency?

A) A configured project connection
B) A model evaluation dataset
C) A prompt variant label
Back:
A) A configured project connection

Project connections define how Foundry applications access dependent Azure and external resources.

Reference: Add connections to a Foundry project
Extra: Evaluation datasets measure behavior, and variant labels distinguish prompt alternatives. Neither establishes resource connectivity or authentication.

Front:
An automation identity needs to create model deployments but must not grant roles to other principals. Which control should enforce this?

A) A custom or built-in RBAC role excluding role-assignment actions
B) Subscription Owner assigned to the automation identity
C) Shared use of a Global Administrator account
Back:
A) A custom or built-in RBAC role excluding role-assignment actions

Least-privilege RBAC can permit resource deployment while withholding Microsoft.Authorization role-assignment permissions.

Reference: Azure role-based access control
Extra: Owner includes access delegation, and shared administrative accounts defeat separation of duties. Scope the role to the resource group or project where possible.

Front:
A pull request changes a model SKU and network setting in Bicep. The team wants to preview Azure resource changes before approval. Which operation should CI run?

A) An Azure Resource Manager what-if deployment
B) A production model inference benchmark only
C) A destructive resource-group deletion test
Back:
A) An Azure Resource Manager what-if deployment

What-if predicts resource additions, removals, and modifications without applying the Bicep deployment.

Reference: Bicep what-if operation
Extra: Inference benchmarks test runtime performance but not infrastructure drift. Destructive tests are unnecessary and unsafe for change preview.

Front:
Clients must keep a stable logical endpoint while a tested model version replaces the old one. Which practice best decouples clients from model versions?

A) Route through a stable deployment or application endpoint name
B) Embed the provider's model version in every client binary
C) Require users to discover a new URL after each release
Back:
A) Route through a stable deployment or application endpoint name

A stable abstraction lets operators change the backing model through a controlled release without coordinating every client.

Reference: Create and deploy Azure OpenAI models
Extra: Hard-coded versions and changing URLs tightly couple clients to releases. Preserve version details in deployment metadata and observability for auditability.

Front:
A model's default safety behavior is insufficient for an application's policy, but the team still needs platform-level filtering at inference. What should be associated with the deployment?

A) A configured content filter policy
B) A higher embedding vector dimension
C) A compute cluster idle shutdown rule
Back:
A) A configured content filter policy

Content filtering can be configured and applied to model deployments to enforce supported harm-category thresholds.

Reference: Configure content filters
Extra: Embedding dimensions affect retrieval representation, and compute shutdown affects cost. Filtering is one defense layer and does not replace application safeguards or evaluation.

Front:
A team needs to compare model offerings, deployment options, task capabilities, and benchmarks before selecting a foundation model. Where should it start?

A) The Foundry model catalog
B) The Azure Policy compliance dashboard
C) The Machine Learning datastore list
Back:
A) The Foundry model catalog

The model catalog supports discovery and comparison of available foundation models and deployment paths.

Reference: Explore the model catalog
Extra: Policy reports governance compliance and datastores list storage connections. Neither supplies model capability and deployment metadata.

Front:
A deployment pipeline must create a Foundry resource, project, and dependent services in a deterministic order. Which design is most maintainable?

A) Modular Bicep with explicit resource dependencies and outputs
B) Independent portal clicks performed in any order
C) One notebook cell containing undocumented REST calls
Back:
A) Modular Bicep with explicit resource dependencies and outputs

Bicep modules and dependency expressions make provisioning order and resource contracts reviewable and repeatable.

Reference: Bicep modules
Extra: Portal operations are manual, and undocumented notebook calls obscure idempotency and failure handling. Module outputs should pass resource identifiers rather than duplicate naming logic.

Front:
A model performs well in English but the production workload includes Spanish and Japanese. What should happen before model selection is finalized?

A) Evaluate candidate models on representative multilingual examples
B) Assume benchmark leadership guarantees equal language quality
C) Translate all outputs after deployment without testing inputs
Back:
A) Evaluate candidate models on representative multilingual examples

Workload-specific evaluation must represent languages, tasks, and distributions expected in production.

Reference: Evaluate models and applications
Extra: Aggregate benchmarks can hide language-specific weaknesses. Post-translation adds another model and does not validate understanding of multilingual inputs.

Front:
A project has separate development and production model deployments. Operators need to know exactly which prompt commit and model version formed each release. What should be recorded?

A) Immutable release metadata linking prompt commit and deployment version
B) Only the current prompt text in a shared document
C) Only the model family name in the resource group tag
Back:
A) Immutable release metadata linking prompt commit and deployment version

Release traceability requires a durable mapping among source, prompt, configuration, model, and deployment versions.

Reference: GenAIOps for generative AI
Extra: A mutable document loses history, while a model family omits prompt and configuration changes. Complete linkage enables rollback and root-cause analysis.

Front:
A customer-facing assistant will be evaluated before release. The team needs examples covering normal requests, edge cases, and known failures with expected context fields. What should it create?

A) A representative versioned test dataset
B) A larger production compute instance
C) A private DNS zone for evaluation results
Back:
A) A representative versioned test dataset

A curated test dataset supplies stable inputs and context for repeatable application and model evaluation.

Reference: Prepare data for evaluation
Extra: Compute size affects execution speed and DNS controls name resolution. Neither defines what quality and risk cases are tested.

Front:
An evaluator expects fields named query, response, and context, but the test file uses question, answer, and passages. What must be configured?

A) Data mapping from dataset columns to evaluator inputs
B) A new provisioned throughput deployment
C) A content filter with higher severity thresholds
Back:
A) Data mapping from dataset columns to evaluator inputs

Evaluation data mapping binds application dataset fields to the evaluator's required input schema.

Reference: Evaluation data mapping
Extra: Throughput and filtering affect serving and safety, not evaluator schema compatibility. Incorrect mapping can produce invalid or misleading scores.

Front:
A RAG assistant gives a fluent answer that contains claims absent from the retrieved documents. Which quality metric most directly exposes the problem?

A) Groundedness
B) Fluency
C) Throughput
Back:
A) Groundedness

Groundedness measures whether response claims are supported by the supplied context.

Reference: Built-in evaluation metrics
Extra: Fluency measures linguistic quality and can be high for fabricated claims. Throughput measures operational capacity, not factual support from retrieved evidence.

Front:
An answer is fully supported by documents but does not address the user's actual question. Which metric should be emphasized?

A) Relevance
B) Groundedness
C) Token consumption
Back:
A) Relevance

Relevance assesses how well the response addresses the user's query and informational need.

Reference: Quality evaluation metrics
Extra: Groundedness can be high for an off-topic but supported statement. Token consumption measures cost and size rather than task alignment.

Front:
A generated report contradicts itself between sections even though each sentence is grammatical. Which metric targets this weakness?

A) Coherence
B) Fluency
C) Request latency
Back:
A) Coherence

Coherence evaluates logical consistency, organization, and meaningful flow across the response.

Reference: Coherence evaluation
Extra: Fluency focuses on language form and readability; latency measures speed. A response can be fluent and fast while logically inconsistent.

Front:
A response contains awkward grammar and unnatural phrasing but follows a logically consistent outline. Which metric best captures the defect?

A) Fluency
B) Coherence
C) Groundedness
Back:
A) Fluency

Fluency measures grammatical correctness, readability, and natural language quality.

Reference: Fluency evaluation
Extra: Coherence evaluates logical structure, while groundedness checks support from context. These quality dimensions should be evaluated separately to avoid masking tradeoffs.

Front:
Before launch, an agent must be tested for hateful, sexual, violent, and self-harm content across adversarial prompts. What evaluation should be run?

A) Risk and safety evaluation
B) Retrieval latency benchmark only
C) Embedding dimensionality analysis
Back:
A) Risk and safety evaluation

Risk and safety evaluators assess supported harmful-content categories and severities in generated interactions.

Reference: Risk and safety evaluators
Extra: Latency and vector dimensions do not measure harmful output. Combine pre-release red-team-style cases, platform controls, and post-release monitoring.

Front:
A legal assistant has a domain rule that citations must use an approved identifier format. No built-in metric checks it. What should the team add?

A) A custom evaluator for citation compliance
B) A larger standard model deployment
C) A lower search similarity threshold
Back:
A) A custom evaluator for citation compliance

Custom evaluators encode application-specific quality rules not covered by general built-in metrics.

Reference: Create custom evaluators
Extra: A larger model may still violate formatting, and search thresholds affect retrieval candidates. Explicit domain metrics make release criteria measurable.

Front:
Every pull request that changes a prompt must run the same evaluation suite and fail when quality drops below thresholds. Where should this run?

A) An automated CI workflow
B) An annual manual production review
C) An interactive notebook with no saved results
Back:
A) An automated CI workflow

CI evaluation provides consistent regression checks before prompt changes merge or deploy.

Reference: Continuous evaluation for generative AI
Extra: Annual review is too late, and unsaved notebook runs are not enforceable or auditable. Version the dataset and evaluator configuration with the release inputs.

Front:
Offline tests pass, but production traffic evolves over time. Which capability should detect ongoing quality changes on sampled live interactions?

A) Continuous monitoring in Foundry
B) A one-time local unit test run
C) A resource-group naming convention
Back:
A) Continuous monitoring in Foundry

Continuous monitoring evaluates operational traces and quality signals after deployment to detect changes in real usage.

Reference: Monitor generative AI applications
Extra: Unit tests remain useful but cannot observe distribution shifts in live traffic. Naming conventions aid organization, not behavioral detection.

Front:
Users report that responses feel slow. Which metric most directly quantifies time from request submission until the response completes?

A) End-to-end response latency
B) Tokens per billing month
C) Groundedness score
Back:
A) End-to-end response latency

End-to-end latency captures user-perceived request duration across retrieval, orchestration, model inference, and post-processing.

Reference: Monitor application performance
Extra: Monthly tokens quantify usage and groundedness measures context support. Trace spans are then needed to identify which stage dominates latency.

Front:
A service meets single-request latency targets but cannot sustain the required requests per minute during peak load. Which metric reveals this limitation?

A) Throughput
B) Coherence
C) Citation precision
Back:
A) Throughput

Throughput measures the amount of work completed per unit time and exposes capacity constraints under load.

Reference: Latency and throughput
Extra: Coherence and citation precision are quality measures. Diagnose throughput alongside rate limits, concurrency, token sizes, and deployment capacity.

Front:
A generative AI application's monthly cost rises although request count is stable. Which telemetry should be examined first?

A) Input and output token consumption by operation
B) Number of Git branches in the prompt repository
C) Count of private DNS records in the virtual network
Back:
A) Input and output token consumption by operation

Token telemetry reveals whether larger prompts, retrieved context, or responses increased model usage per request.

Reference: Monitor cost and token usage
Extra: Source branches and DNS records do not drive model token billing. Correlate tokens with model deployment, route, customer, and prompt version to locate regressions.

Front:
An agent intermittently calls the wrong tool. Operators need to reconstruct model calls, tool calls, timing, and errors for one request. What should be enabled?

A) Distributed tracing with correlated spans and detailed logs
B) Only aggregate monthly token totals
C) Only Azure Resource Manager activity logs
Back:
A) Distributed tracing with correlated spans and detailed logs

Traces show the sequence and timing of application, model, retrieval, and tool operations for a request.

Reference: Trace generative AI applications
Extra: Aggregate totals lack request detail, while activity logs record management-plane changes rather than agent execution. Redact sensitive prompt and tool data according to policy.

Front:
A release dashboard shows average latency is acceptable, but a small group experiences severe delays. Which analysis should be added?

A) Tail latency percentiles such as p95 and p99
B) Only the arithmetic mean latency
C) Only the total number of model deployments
Back:
A) Tail latency percentiles such as p95 and p99

High percentiles reveal slow outliers hidden by an acceptable average and better represent poor user experiences.

Reference: Performance testing guidance
Extra: The mean can conceal a long tail, and deployment counts say nothing about request duration. Segment percentiles by model, route, region, and prompt version.

Front:
RAG retrieval returns many weakly related passages that distract the model. Relevant documents usually score much higher. What should be tuned first?

A) Raise the similarity threshold using evaluation evidence
B) Increase response temperature for more variety
C) Increase model output-token allowance
Back:
A) Raise the similarity threshold using evaluation evidence

A higher similarity cutoff can exclude low-relevance retrieval results when score separation supports that choice.

Reference: Vector query configuration
Extra: Temperature and output limits affect generation, not which passages are retrieved. Tune thresholds against recall and relevance because an excessive cutoff can omit needed evidence.

Front:
Large documents are indexed as entire files, causing broad embeddings and oversized context. Which change is most likely to improve retrieval precision?

A) Split documents into semantically meaningful chunks with controlled overlap
B) Concatenate all documents into one index record
C) Remove document metadata before indexing
Back:
A) Split documents into semantically meaningful chunks with controlled overlap

Chunking creates focused retrieval units while overlap can preserve concepts crossing boundaries.

Reference: Chunk documents for vector search
Extra: A single record reduces granularity, and removing metadata discards useful filtering and citation context. Evaluate chunk size rather than assuming smaller is always better.

Front:
A RAG system retrieves one excellent passage but often misses a second passage needed to answer multi-part questions. Which parameter should be evaluated?

A) The number of top results returned
B) The model's maximum output tokens only
C) The deployment's content filter severity only
Back:
A) The number of top results returned

Increasing top-k can improve retrieval recall for questions requiring evidence from multiple chunks.

Reference: Configure vector query results
Extra: Generation limits and content filters do not add retrieved evidence. Larger top-k can add noise and cost, so tune it with end-to-end relevance evaluation.

Front:
A multilingual legal corpus uses specialized terminology. The current general embedding model performs poorly on cross-language retrieval. What is the best next step?

A) Evaluate multilingual or domain-suitable embedding models on labeled query-document pairs
B) Select an embedding model solely by its vector dimension
C) Increase the chat model temperature during retrieval
Back:
A) Evaluate multilingual or domain-suitable embedding models on labeled query-document pairs

Embedding selection should be based on retrieval quality for representative languages and domain semantics.

Reference: Select models in Foundry
Extra: Dimension affects storage and compatibility but does not prove relevance. Chat temperature applies during generation and cannot repair the embedding space.

Front:
An embedding model is adapted for a medical vocabulary. What must happen before it replaces the production embedding model?

A) Re-embed indexed content and validate queries in a compatible index
B) Keep old document vectors and change only query embeddings
C) Change the chat model without touching the search index
Back:
A) Re-embed indexed content and validate queries in a compatible index

Queries and documents must be encoded into the same compatible embedding space for meaningful vector similarity.

Reference: Create a vector index
Extra: Mixing old document vectors with new query embeddings yields invalid similarity comparisons. Use a parallel index for safe evaluation and rollback.

Front:
Users search with exact product codes plus natural-language descriptions. Which retrieval design best combines lexical precision and semantic similarity?

A) Hybrid search with keyword and vector queries
B) Vector search with all text fields removed
C) Keyword search with embeddings disabled permanently
Back:
A) Hybrid search with keyword and vector queries

Hybrid search executes lexical and vector retrieval together and merges their results.

Reference: Hybrid search overview
Extra: Vector-only retrieval can miss exact identifiers, while keyword-only retrieval can miss paraphrases. Hybrid retrieval is especially useful when both behaviors matter.

Front:
Hybrid retrieval returns a strong candidate set, but ranking still poorly reflects the meaning of complex natural-language questions. Which feature can rerank the results?

A) Semantic ranker
B) Storage lifecycle management
C) Compute instance autostop
Back:
A) Semantic ranker

Semantic ranker applies language understanding to rerank an initial search result set for semantic relevance.

Reference: Semantic ranking in Azure AI Search
Extra: Storage lifecycle and compute schedules control cost, not search ordering. Semantic ranking complements retrieval and does not replace a well-designed index or filters.

Front:
A team changes chunk size and retrieval strategy. Which evaluation most directly determines whether the retriever improved before generation?

A) Retrieval relevance metrics on labeled query-document judgments
B) GPU utilization of the chat model deployment
C) Grammatical fluency of generated answers only
Back:
A) Retrieval relevance metrics on labeled query-document judgments

Retriever metrics compare returned documents with relevance judgments and isolate search quality from generation behavior.

Reference: Retrieval evaluation metrics
Extra: GPU utilization is operational, and answer fluency can remain high with poor evidence. Also run end-to-end groundedness and relevance tests before release.

Front:
Two RAG configurations pass offline tests. The team needs evidence from real users while limiting risk. Which experiment is appropriate?

A) A randomized A/B test with predefined success and guardrail metrics
B) A full replacement with no control group
C) A comparison of configuration file lengths
Back:
A) A randomized A/B test with predefined success and guardrail metrics

A controlled A/B test estimates causal performance differences while monitoring quality, safety, latency, and cost.

Reference: GenAIOps experimentation
Extra: Full replacement confounds change with time and raises blast radius. File length has no reliable relationship to user outcomes.

Front:
A base model follows general instructions but repeatedly mishandles a stable, specialized output task despite prompt optimization and sufficient examples. Which customization may help?

A) Supervised fine-tuning with curated input-output examples
B) Increasing search replicas without using retrieval
C) Adding more private DNS records to the project
Back:
A) Supervised fine-tuning with curated input-output examples

Supervised fine-tuning can adapt model behavior to a recurring task using high-quality labeled demonstrations.

Reference: Fine-tuning considerations
Extra: Search capacity and DNS do not teach model behavior. Fine-tuning should follow prompt and RAG baselines because it adds data, evaluation, cost, and lifecycle obligations.

Front:
A fine-tuning project lacks enough examples of rare but important cases. The team plans to generate synthetic examples. Which practice is essential?

A) Validate synthetic data for correctness, diversity, and leakage before training
B) Accept every generated example without review
C) Replace the real validation set with synthetic training data
Back:
A) Validate synthetic data for correctness, diversity, and leakage before training

Synthetic data can expand coverage but requires quality controls to avoid amplifying errors, bias, duplication, or contamination.

Reference: Synthetic data generation
Extra: Unreviewed examples can teach false patterns. Keep an independent representative validation set so evaluation does not merely reward synthetic artifacts.

Front:
A fine-tuned model improves task accuracy but doubles latency and increases harmful-output failures. What should determine promotion?

A) A multi-metric gate covering quality, safety, latency, and cost
B) Task accuracy alone regardless of regressions
C) The number of completed training epochs alone
Back:
A) A multi-metric gate covering quality, safety, latency, and cost

Production readiness is a constrained optimization problem; improvement in one metric cannot excuse failed operational or safety requirements.

Reference: Deploy and evaluate fine-tuned models
Extra: Accuracy and epoch count are insufficient decision criteria. Define thresholds before training and compare against the base-model baseline on identical tests.

Front:
A new fine-tuned model version is approved, but production rollback must remain immediate. Which release approach is best?

A) Register and deploy it as a separate version, then shift traffic gradually
B) Overwrite the only production model artifact in place
C) Delete the prior deployment before testing the new model
Back:
A) Register and deploy it as a separate version, then shift traffic gradually

Separate immutable versions support controlled promotion, comparison, traceability, and rapid rollback.

Reference: Deploy a fine-tuned model
Extra: In-place overwrite and early deletion remove the known-good rollback target. Keep training data, hyperparameters, base model, evaluations, and deployment metadata linked to each version.
